knowledge.the_winter_rescue.earthen_smel: Copper and tin minerals suggest using clay and sand to build a smelter. Try linking a raw copper observation; clay ball and sand observations make the puzzle easier.

Craft three mixtures of Unfired Trial Kiln, fire them and compare the samples to find a suitable furnace material.
Finishing unlocks earthen kiln bricks and smelter construction with an engineer hammer. Find the kilns and material recipes in JEI.
Link a raw copper observation. Learned clay ball and sand observations each remove one ordered number from the puzzle; placing them on the tray is also allowed.
Submit this run's intact trial kiln (consumes one)
You can now craft earthen kiln bricks using the existing bricks and structural metal plate recipe. Trial kilns are not an ingredient.

Arrange earthen kiln bricks in the multiblock pattern and form it with an engineer hammer. Finishing this research normally also learns Earthen Kiln Brick Design automatically, unlocking the brick recipe at the same time.
knowledge.the_winter_rescue.iron_bloomer: An Idea for Iron Smelting

Iron minerals and products suggest that stronger airflow may help smelt iron. Try linking raw iron with coal, charcoal or coke observations; copper or bronze ingot observations make the puzzle easier.
Bloomery

Plan an air passage at the drawing desk, then craft a Prototype Tuyere, test it with a bellows and observe the resulting Sandy Brick Tuyere.
Finishing unlocks the bloomery and regular tuyere recipes. The prototype recipe becomes available after planning the passage; find it in JEI.
Learned copper or bronze ingot observation
Learned coal, charcoal or coke observation
Iron minerals or common iron products
Link raw iron and one fuel observation. A learned copper or bronze ingot observation removes one ordered number from the puzzle; placing it on the tray is also allowed.
Bloomery and Tuyere Design

This result is normally learned automatically on completion, unlocking both main bloomery and sandy tuyere recipes. Manually learn it only if it actually remains unlearned in the inbox. Prepare sandy bricks, bronze plates and mortar.
Plan the Airflow
Send cool air through the charcoal bed and out the furnace top

Click Plan Air Passage below. Starting at the small inlet cavity, hold and drag the left mouse button to carve through the sandy bricks. Lead air through the charcoal bed to the upper outlet. If cold air escapes through another boundary first, reset and try again.
After success, return to research and click Enter Next Stage to test the tuyere.
Air has crossed the charcoal bed and exited at the furnace top. The prototype recipe is temporarily available; advance to the next stage.
Plan the charcoal-bed airflow
Test the Tuyere
Build and test a Prototype Tuyere

1. Craft a Prototype Tuyere from 1 block of Sandy Bricks, 1 bronze plate and 1 mortar; see JEI for the recipe.
2. Place it one block in front of the bellows outlet. Operate the bellows until it becomes a Sandy Brick Tuyere. Place the prototype after entering this stage; pick up and replace any prototype placed earlier.
The tuyere has passed its airflow trial. Finish research to build a bloomery.
Observe the tested Sandy Brick Tuyere in place
knowledge.the_winter_rescue.refractory_b: An Idea for Refractory Firing

These materials and refractory products suggest improving bricks through controlled firing. Try linking an item observation of a sandy brick or sandy brick block; kaolin, bauxite and clay ball observations make the puzzle easier.
Ordinary Refractory Bricks

Build a Controlled Furnace and fire Fire Clay Balls at different temperatures. Observe the resulting Refractory Brick to find a suitable firing method.
Finishing unlocks batch brick production in this furnace. Find equipment and material recipes in JEI.
Learned a kaolin material observation
Learned a bauxite material observation
Learned clay ball observation

Link an item observation of a sandy brick or sandy brick block. Learned kaolin, bauxite and clay ball observations each remove one ordered number; placing them on the tray is also allowed. Each material group counts once.
Controlled Refractory Batch Production

Normally learned automatically, this design enables 16 fire clay balls and 2 charcoal to produce 16 ordinary refractory bricks in the controlled furnace. It only unlocks the new batch process. Existing pottery, blast furnace, industrial kiln and block recipes remain unchanged. It does not unlock high refractory bricks or the IE blast furnace.
Prepare Materials and Equipment
Prepare a Fire Clay Ball, charcoal and a Controlled Furnace

1. Prepare the powders. Thaw frozen kaolin and bauxite at a campfire. Break bauxite with a stone hammer on a stump, then grind it on a millstone; kaolin can be ground directly.
2. Mix 4 kaolin dust, 4 bauxite dust and 1 clay ball in a crafting table to make a Fire Clay Ball.
3. Craft a Controlled Furnace from 6 clay balls, 2 sand and 1 campfire; see JEI for the layout. Bring 1 charcoal.
When ready, click Enter Next Stage to begin firing.
You can begin firing. Observing an existing refractory brick helps narrow the temperature range.
Fire and Observe
Test-fire a brick in the Controlled Furnace

1. Open the Controlled Furnace, select Trial mode and insert 1 Fire Clay Ball and 1 charcoal.
2. Try a temperature between 1000 and 1200 C; 1100 C is a useful starting point. Click Start, wait 20 seconds and collect the sample. If it is a Cracked Refractory Brick, adjust the temperature and try again with fresh materials.

1. Open the Controlled Furnace, select Trial mode and insert 1 Fire Clay Ball and 1 charcoal.
2. Your existing brick observations suggest 1050 to 1150 C, inclusive; try 1100 C. Click Start, wait 20 seconds and collect the sample.
The ordinary refractory brick has passed its trial. Finish research to enable batch production.
Observe the intact Refractory Brick from this trial
